top_10.title: Agent message persistence commits SQLite synchronously on the controller loop
top_10.body:
Part of the #2706 family (SQLite work on the controller loop). Found in the v3.2.1 post-tag upgrade run on a slow disk. Present since at least 3.2.0. Targets 3.2.2.

## Evidence

On the first Turn after the migration, the loop stalled for 3.0 s, 2.8 s and 3.9 s. The loop thread's stack, innermost frames last:

```
modules/agents/vibey/agent.py _settle → base.emit_result_message
core/controller.py emit_agent_message
core/message_dispatcher.py emit_agent_message → persist_agent_message
core/message_mirror.py persist_agent_message: with engine.begin() as conn
sqlalchemy ... do_commit → dbapi_connection.commit()
```

The wait is in the **commit** itself, not in acquiring SQLite's writer. On a slow disk, a commit's `fsync`, plus any WAL auto-checkpoint the commit triggers, runs synchronously on the loop thread. The test install's database was only 840 KB, which points at `fsync` latency rather than a large checkpoint.

## Why it is not a simple move to a thread (the #2708 check)

`persist_agent_message` runs for every persisted output: results, notices, interim rows, and hosted/tool-call trace rows. It runs on the loop today, so persists commit in the order the loop issued them. Two loop sections depend on that order:

1. **Within one emit.** The emit uses the persisted row (`persisted_output`): its id feeds delivery evidence and the Run's terminal record (`message_id`). Awaiting an off-loop persist in place keeps this order.
2. **Across concurrent emits for the same Session.** For example, a receiver's result and a concurrent Activity-output flush. The transaction assigns the row's position and transcript rank (`rank`, `message.new`, inbox). On the runtime-work executor, which has several threads, two persists could commit in the opposite order from the one the loop issued them in, and the transcript order would change.

The ordering requirement rules out the general door as is: transcript order must stay loop order.

## Proposed shape

Persist through an **ordered writer**: a single-thread executor that commits persists in the order the loop submitted them. Each emit awaits its own persist under the `_store_step` rule (#2715), so cancellation points stay where they are on master.

The post-commit publishes (`message.new`, `inbox.session.updated`, activity) go out from the loop after the commit lands, in the same order.

`persist_silent_terminal` and the other `message_mirror` writers go through the same writer.

## Placement

Right after path A (#2715), as A2: same emit path, same cancellation rule. Before B step 2. A short design check on the ordered writer comes first, covering:
- that cross-Session order needs no stronger guarantee than per-submission order;
- how the writer drains at shutdown;
- the plan-test-style regression: a held writer must not hold the loop, and two concurrent emits must keep their order.

top_10.title: [yaxuanm/qdrant] Hybrid Search fails on named-vector collections (dense/sparse)
top_10.body:
## Plugin
yaxuanm/qdrant v0.0.1

## Problem
Hybrid Search fails on collections with named vectors (`dense`, `sparse`) created outside the plugin (e.g. custom embed scripts).
**Error:** Qdrant responded with HTTP 400: Wrong input: Not existing vector name error:


## Root cause
1. Operation inference checks `text` before hybrid indicators → runs `operation: "query"` instead of `hybrid_search`
2. Plain query sends unnamed `vector` to `/points/search` — invalid when collection has only named vectors
3. Sparse vector is not generated from `text` in hybrid path (only dense embedding is created)
## Reproduction
- Collection: named vectors `dense` (3072) + `sparse`
- Tool: Qdrant · Hybrid Search
- Inputs: `text`, `using_dense: dense`, `using_sparse: sparse`, `fusion_method: rrf`
- Embedding: text-embedding-3-large
## Expected
`hybrid_search` → `/points/query` with prefetch using `dense` and `sparse`
## Actual
`query` → `/points/search` with flat `vector` array (no vector name)
## Fix verified locally (v0.0.2)
- Route hybrid before text→query
- Set `operation: hybrid_search` on hybrid tool YAML
- Generate sparse via `fastembed` (`Qdrant/bm25`)
- Add `fastembed` dependency
## Environment
- Dify 1.14.2 (self-hosted)
- Qdrant Cloud
- Plugin: yaxuanm/qdrant 0.0.1 from Marketplace

### Plugin Name

Hive

### Function Description

Social media management inside a Dify workflow: publish and schedule across twelve networks, read cross-account analytics, work a shared inbox, and build DM automations for Instagram, Messenger, WhatsApp and TikTok.

Scenarios people would build:
- An agent drafts a post, validates it against each network's rules, and schedules it
- A scheduled workflow pulls last week's numbers across every connected account and writes a summary
- A form submission becomes an idea on the content board

Everything needed to build the plugin is already published:

- **OpenAPI 3.1**: https://hivepublish.com/api/v1/openapi.json — 50 endpoints, one per tool, each with an operationId, responses and a description

top_10.title: [Plugin Request]: Baizhi Agent Toolkit - web search, scraping, and extraction
top_10.body:
### Plugin Name

Baizhi Agent Toolkit

### Function Description

Hi Dify team,

I maintain Baizhi Cloud's Agent Toolkit integrations and coordinate product operations. I am submitting this request through `ct-jaryn` on behalf of Baizhi Cloud. We would like to contribute and maintain a native Tool Plugin, and would appreciate feedback on whether the following scope fits the Marketplace's expectations for a distinct integration.

Baizhi Agent Toolkit is a hosted commercial tool service, not an LLM inference provider. Users need their own Baizhi account and API key; tool calls can consume service credits. Our [official integration repository](https://github.com/chaitin/baizhi-agent-toolkit) publishes integration configuration, documentation, and tests, not the hosted backend implementation.

The proposed plugin itself would be free and open source; Baizhi's hosted service usage would be billed separately under its service terms.

#### Proposed user experience

Install the plugin, authorize it with a required provider-level `secret-input` and a link to the [Baizhi console](https://agent-toolkit.app.baizhi.cloud/), then select one of three typed tools in a Workflow or Agent:

- **Web search** (`websearch_search`): search public web sources with query, freshness, result-count, and source-filter parameters.
- **Read a web page** (`web_scrape`): retrieve a page's content from a user-supplied HTTP(S) URL.
- **Extract structured information** (`web_extract`): request specified fields or instruction-driven extraction from a page.

The plugin would use a fixed Streamable HTTP endpoint, `https://agent-toolkit.app.baizhi.cloud/mcp`, with `Authorization: Bearer <user-provided key>`. The credential would not be a model-supplied tool parameter. Public examples, source code, packages, and CI would contain no real key.

#### Difference from existing MCP support

Dify already supports remote MCP and custom headers, and the Marketplace already has general-purpose MCP clients. We are not requesting another generic MCP connector or claiming that native MCP support is missing.

The intended contribution is a service-specific provider credential flow and three stable, typed workflow tools, with maintained parameter/output mapping, bounded errors, documentation, and compatibility tests. The plugin would not accept arbitrary remote tool names or automatically expose newly discovered capabilities. Provider credential validation would use initialization and tool discovery only, not a billable tool invocation. This needs to earn its place as a focused integration rather than merely rebrand a generic client.

#### Safety and review scope

Although the plugin's own MCP connection has a fixed destination, page scraping and extraction delegate user-supplied URL retrieval to the hosted service. We would conservatively disclose **High risk** under the current arbitrary-URL-fetching/crawling criteria, document request timeouts and data flow, and not infer low risk from the fixed transport endpoint. No code execution, shell access, cloud sandbox, payment, or arbitrary-tool forwarding is proposed.

The plugin would need an accurate privacy policy covering the data sent to Baizhi and relevant downstream services, plus credential/logging safeguards. We will not invent data-retention, residency, or no-logging guarantees. The adapter's open-source license and the hosted service's account/usage terms would be disclosed separately.

#### Contribution status and next steps

We have completed a local three-tool prototype from a previously recorded, credential-free tool-schema snapshot. Its 55 offline tests pass with the actual Dify and MCP SDKs and in-memory HTTP transports; a separate local review and rerun also passed. The tests cover provider declarations, typed input mapping, discovery-only credential checks, the fixed endpoint, redirect rejection, bounded discovery, and credential/error/log redaction. These are local results; reviewable source and release artifacts have not yet been published.

The prototype has not been accepted into the Marketplace, validated in a real Dify Community Edition or Cloud workspace, or newly tested against the production service. Historical schemas may have changed. URL validation is not a complete server-side request-forgery defense, and a post-parse output-size check is not a strict transport-memory bound. This issue remains a plugin-scope request, **not a packaged submission or a completed compatibility claim**.

Before a release PR, we would publish reviewable plugin source and setup/troubleshooting documentation, verify current tool schemas and a limited live flow with a dedicated revocable key, complete Dify installation/credential/tool tests, confirm the privacy disclosure and Developer Agreement, and submit one validated `.difypkg` through this repository's current template. Agreement and unperformed-test checkboxes will not be pre-checked.

We would welcome guidance if an existing integration or a different contribution route is more appropriate. Thank you for considering the proposal; the Baizhi team would be glad to cooperate on a maintainable integration that fits Dify's architecture and review standards. This request does not imply Dify endorsement or an established partnership.

### Official Website URL

https://baizhi.cloud/landing/agent-toolkit

top_10.title: [Plugin Request]: AnySearch — unified general + vertical AI search
top_10.body:
### Plugin Name

AnySearch

### Function Description

**API Docs**

API base: `https://api.anysearch.com` · MCP: `https://api.anysearch.com/mcp`

**Function Description**

AnySearch is a unified search API built for AI agents: one endpoint serving both general web search and vertical, structured data retrieval. We would like to publish it as a community tool plugin in the `search` category (`tags: [search]`, same shape as the official Tavily / Brave providers), and we would rather confirm with the maintainers first that it is welcome alongside the existing search providers — and whether you would prefer a different tag, scope, or risk framing.

**Proposed plugin surface** — three tools, Python 3.12 runner, minimal dependency footprint (`requests` only):

| Tool | Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `anysearch_search` | `POST /v1/search` | Unified search. `query` (required), `tag` (`{domain}.{sub_domain}`, e.g. `code.doc`), `params` (object, tag-specific, e.g. `{"ticker":"AAPL"}`), `zone` (`cn` / `intl`), `language`, `max_results` (1–10), `format` (`json` / `markdown`) |
| `anysearch_capabilities` | `GET /v1/sub-domains` | Returns available domains, capability tags and their parameter definitions. Does **not** consume search quota. |
| `anysearch_extract` | `POST /v1/extract` | Fetch and extract clean content (HTML / plain text / JSON / Markdown) from a public URL |

The provider credential would be a `secret-input` API key that is **optional**: unauthenticated calls work against a per-IP rate-limited daily free tier, so users — and reviewers — can evaluate the plugin before signing up. Authenticated calls use `Authorization: Bearer <key>` against a paid quota.

**Why this is not a duplicate of the existing search providers**

The official providers are either general web search (Google, Bing, Brave, DuckDuckGo, Tavily, Serper, SearchApi, SearXNG, Perplexity) or extract/crawl (Jina, Firecrawl). The community vertical ones are single-purpose and region-bound (Google Scholar, Bilibili Search, Webz News Search, Bocha, Baidu AI Search, ZhipuAI Web Search). AnySearch differs on these specific points:

1. **General and vertical from the same endpoint and the same key.** A plain call behaves like general web search; adding `tag=finance.quote` with `params={"type":"crypto"}` returns live market quotes instead of blue links. No second vendor, no second credential, no second plugin.
2. **The vertical catalog is data, not a build-time schema.** `GET /v1/sub-domains` returns the available domains, tags and parameter definitions (`description`, `required`, `sort_order`) at runtime, at no quota cost. The plugin surface therefore stays at three tools as the catalog grows, instead of needing a new tool or plugin release per vertical.
3. **Intent routing and result fusion.** Per our docs, `/v1/search` routes the query to the best underlying sources by intent and then fuses and re-ranks the results — the caller does not pick an engine or merge result sets by hand.
4. **Region routing.** `zone: cn | intl` selects the result universe inside one API, instead of needing separate CN and global plugins.
5. **No-key first run.** Verified: an anonymous `POST /v1/search` returns `code: 0` with results, so a user can try the tool before creating an account.
6. **Low integration cost.** An MCP server is already live over Streamable HTTP at `https://api.anysearch.com/mcp` (anonymous or Bearer), and a Skill package already exists — the native tool plugin can be built and reviewed against a working endpoint rather than a spec.

**Questions for the maintainers** — we would rather ask before opening the PR:

1. **Category / overlap.** We could not find a published policy on category overlap (`CONTRIBUTING.md` is still `TODO`). Is another `search`-tagged provider welcome, or would you prefer it under a distinct tag or label to keep the category legible?
2. **Optional credentials.** Is an optional API key acceptable for a search-category provider, given that most existing providers require one? If not, we will make the key required and drop the anonymous path in the plugin.
3. **Risk classification.** `POST /v1/extract` fetches user-supplied URLs. Reading `docs/plugin-submission-requirements.md`, we believe that places the plugin at High risk ("proxy or crawl arbitrary URLs"). We intend to declare High and constrain inputs, set request timeouts, and avoid leaking credentials in errors. Please confirm that is the level you expect, and whether a High-risk plugin in the search category is acceptable.
4. **Exposed tag set.** The live catalog is broader than what a typical Dify user needs, and includes health, financial and legal data alongside some legally sensitive sources. We are happy to restrict the tag set the plugin exposes. Would you like us to, and do you have guidance on which verticals a search provider in the Marketplace should surface?
5. **Listing path.** We assume the expected route is a PR to `langgenius/dify-plugins` adding `anysearch/anysearch/anysearch-<version>.difypkg`, with `PRIVACY.md`, a source-repository link and an English README. If you would instead prefer to handle AnySearch as an official / featured integration, or an MCP-only listing, tell us and we will follow that path.

We are happy to adjust scope to whatever keeps the Marketplace coherent. Thanks.

### Official Website URL

https://anysearch.com/docs

top_10.title: Kubernetes sandbox backend (no Docker socket)
top_10.body:
## Problem

Every sandbox starts a sibling container through the `docker` CLI and
`/var/run/docker.sock`. That covers Agent Python tools and skills, the Code
node and its formatter, custom Playwright, MCP stdio, and the Codex and
OpenCode wrappers.

Some Kubernetes nodes have no Docker daemon: Talos, Bottlerocket,
containerd-only pools on EKS, AKS and GKE, and OpenShift. There, the only
choice is `HEYM_*_SANDBOX=subprocess`, which the docs call trusted
single-user only, or nothing. The Code node, Codex and OpenCode have no
fallback and fail.

## Who hits it

Anyone self-hosting Heym on Kubernetes, where mounting the host's Docker
socket is either impossible or not something you would want to do.

## Proposed approach

Three PRs, each releasable on its own:

1. **No behaviour change.** Move the nine `docker run` builders behind one
   `SandboxSpec` plus a `DockerRunner`. Parity tests assert that the argv
   stays the same, flag for flag. This also removes the five copies of
   `_docker_available`, `_resolve_image` and `_force_remove_container`.
2. **`HEYM_SANDBOX_BACKEND=kubernetes`, for the stdin/stdout-only sites:**
   the Python tool, the Code formatter, the Code node without requirements,
   and Playwright.
    - Each run is one Pod in a configurable namespace, under Pod Security
      `restricted`, with no ServiceAccount token.
    - `--network none|bridge` becomes a pod label that operator-provided
      NetworkPolicies select.
    - It is built on `httpx` and `websockets`, so there is no new dependency.
    - It fails closed exactly as the Docker path does.
3. **Workspaces.** Skills, Code node requirements and MCP stdio first, then
   Codex and OpenCode. There are two modes, and each run sees only its own
   files in both:
    - `stream` (default): a tar over the pod's attach stream, the same way
      `kubectl cp` moves files. No storage needed.
    - `volume`: an RWX PVC mounted with `subPath` set to the run's directory,
      the Kubernetes equivalent of today's `volume-subpath`.

Docker stays the default. No schema, migration, UI or public API changes.

## Touches

- `backend/app/services/*_executor.py`
- `mcp_stdio_sandbox.py`
- `playwright_sandbox.py`
- `code_formatter.py`
- `docker/heym-*-docker`
- `ENVIRONMENT-VARIABLES.md`

## Questions

1. Do you want a Kubernetes backend in-tree, or would you rather Docker stay
   the only supported sandbox?
2. Is the `SandboxSpec` plus runner shape right for PR 1? I'd rather agree on
   it here than in a large diff.
3. Codex's bubblewrap cannot run in a `restricted` pod. Is
   `--sandbox danger-full-access` acceptable when the pod is the boundary?
4. Would a Helm chart help, either in-tree under `deploy/helm/` or as a
   separate community chart on Artifact Hub? It would package Heym plus the
   sandbox namespace, RBAC and NetworkPolicies, with presets for OpenShift,
   EKS, AKS and GKE. I'd maintain it, including tag bumps.

I have a prototype that matches the current argv of all nine call sites and
am happy to share it. I'll wait for your go-ahead on scope, and can talk it
through on Discord first if that's easier.

top_10.title: Flagship eval did not pass on v0.25.4-rc1
top_10.body:
The flagship eval on release tag `v0.25.4-rc1` did not pass. Publishing is not blocked by it.

- Run: https://github.com/amd/gaia/actions/runs/41148504198
- Tier: `smoke` (eval/ci_tiers.json)
- Scenario lanes: `failure`
- Outcomes (`gaia eval tasks`): `skipped`
- Final tag, full sweep found for this commit or an RC: `skipped` (`skipped` on an RC)

Start with the run's summary page: it names which lanes measured, which measured nothing, and
how long each took. Then download the failing lane's `eval-<lane>` artifact - it carries the
transcripts, judge rationales, backend log and Lemonade logs. Those machines are ephemeral and
already destroyed, so the artifact is the only copy, and it expires in 14 days.

Compare with the previous tag's run first. A failure no change since then explains usually means
the environment moved, not the code: a Lemonade version bump, a re-quantised model, a driver or
runner-image change.

`cancelled` rather than `failure` means no measurement happened at all - a manual cancel, or a
lane that waited out GitHub's 24h queue limit. Re-dispatch the workflow on the tag.

A passing re-run closes this issue, and so does a later passing tag on the same major.minor line
whose tier covers this one (a full sweep covers smoke). A final tag's issue closes only on its own
passing re-run.

Install the plugin, authorize it with a required provider-level `secret-input` and a link to the [Baizhi console](https://agent-toolkit.app.baizhi.cloud/), then select one of three typed tools in a Workflow or Agent:

- **Web search** (`websearch_search`): search public web sources with query, freshness, result-count, and source-filter parameters.
- **Read a web page** (`web_scrape`): retrieve a page's content from a user-supplied HTTP(S) URL.
- **Extract structured information** (`web_extract`): request specified fields or instruction-driven extraction from a page.

The plugin would use a fixed Streamable HTTP endpoint, `https://agent-toolkit.app.baizhi.cloud/mcp`, with `Authorization: Bearer <user-provided key>`. The credential would not be a model-supplied tool parameter. Public examples, source code, packages, and CI would contain no real key.

#### Difference from existing MCP support

Dify already supports remote MCP and custom headers, and the Marketplace already has general-purpose MCP clients. We are not requesting another generic MCP connector or claiming that native MCP support is missing.

The intended contribution is a service-specific provider credential flow and three stable, typed workflow tools, with maintained parameter/output mapping, bounded errors, documentation, and compatibility tests. The plugin would not accept arbitrary remote tool names or automatically expose newly discovered capabilities. Provider credential validation would use initialization and tool discovery only, not a billable tool invocation. This needs to earn its place as a focused integration rather than merely rebrand a generic client.

#### Safety and review scope

Although the plugin's own MCP connection has a fixed destination, page scraping and extraction delegate user-supplied URL retrieval to the hosted service. We would conservatively disclose **High risk** under the current arbitrary-URL-fetching/crawling criteria, document request timeouts and data flow, and not infer low risk from the fixed transport endpoint. No code execution, shell access, cloud sandbox, payment, or arbitrary-tool forwarding is proposed.

The plugin would need an accurate privacy policy covering the data sent to Baizhi and relevant downstream services, plus credential/logging safeguards. We will not invent data-retention, residency, or no-logging guarantees. The adapter's open-source license and the hosted service's account/usage terms would be disclosed separately.

#### Contribution status and next steps

We have completed a local three-tool prototype from a previously recorded, credential-free tool-schema snapshot. Its 55 offline tests pass with the actual Dify and MCP SDKs and in-memory HTTP transports; a separate local review and rerun also passed. The tests cover provider declarations, typed input mapping, discovery-only credential checks, the fixed endpoint, redirect rejection, bounded discovery, and credential/error/log redaction. These are local results; reviewable source and release artifacts have not yet been published.

The prototype has not been accepted into the Marketplace, validated in a real Dify Community Edition or Cloud workspace, or newly tested against the production service. Historical schemas may have changed. URL validation is not a complete server-side request-forgery defense, and a post-parse output-size check is not a strict transport-memory bound. This issue remains a plugin-scope request, **not a packaged submission or a completed compatibility claim**.

Before a release PR, we would publish reviewable plugin source and setup/troubleshooting documentation, verify current tool schemas and a limited live flow with a dedicated revocable key, complete Dify installation/credential/tool tests, confirm the privacy disclosure and Developer Agreement, and submit one validated `.difypkg` through this repository's current template. Agreement and unperformed-test checkboxes will not be pre-checked.

We would welcome guidance if an existing integration or a different contribution route is more appropriate. Thank you for considering the proposal; the Baizhi team would be glad to cooperate on a maintainable integration that fits Dify's architecture and review standards. This request does not imply Dify endorsement or an established partnership.

issues.title: [Plugin Request]: AnySearch — unified general + vertical AI search
issues.body:
### Plugin Name

AnySearch

### Function Description

**API Docs**

API base: `https://api.anysearch.com` · MCP: `https://api.anysearch.com/mcp`

**Function Description**

AnySearch is a unified search API built for AI agents: one endpoint serving both general web search and vertical, structured data retrieval. We would like to publish it as a community tool plugin in the `search` category (`tags: [search]`, same shape as the official Tavily / Brave providers), and we would rather confirm with the maintainers first that it is welcome alongside the existing search providers — and whether you would prefer a different tag, scope, or risk framing.

**Proposed plugin surface** — three tools, Python 3.12 runner, minimal dependency footprint (`requests` only):

| Tool | Endpoint | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `anysearch_search` | `POST /v1/search` | Unified search. `query` (required), `tag` (`{domain}.{sub_domain}`, e.g. `code.doc`), `params` (object, tag-specific, e.g. `{"ticker":"AAPL"}`), `zone` (`cn` / `intl`), `language`, `max_results` (1–10), `format` (`json` / `markdown`) |
| `anysearch_capabilities` | `GET /v1/sub-domains` | Returns available domains, capability tags and their parameter definitions. Does **not** consume search quota. |
| `anysearch_extract` | `POST /v1/extract` | Fetch and extract clean content (HTML / plain text / JSON / Markdown) from a public URL |

The provider credential would be a `secret-input` API key that is **optional**: unauthenticated calls work against a per-IP rate-limited daily free tier, so users — and reviewers — can evaluate the plugin before signing up. Authenticated calls use `Authorization: Bearer <key>` against a paid quota.

**Why this is not a duplicate of the existing search providers**

The official providers are either general web search (Google, Bing, Brave, DuckDuckGo, Tavily, Serper, SearchApi, SearXNG, Perplexity) or extract/crawl (Jina, Firecrawl). The community vertical ones are single-purpose and region-bound (Google Scholar, Bilibili Search, Webz News Search, Bocha, Baidu AI Search, ZhipuAI Web Search). AnySearch differs on these specific points:

1. **General and vertical from the same endpoint and the same key.** A plain call behaves like general web search; adding `tag=finance.quote` with `params={"type":"crypto"}` returns live market quotes instead of blue links. No second vendor, no second credential, no second plugin.
2. **The vertical catalog is data, not a build-time schema.** `GET /v1/sub-domains` returns the available domains, tags and parameter definitions (`description`, `required`, `sort_order`) at runtime, at no quota cost. The plugin surface therefore stays at three tools as the catalog grows, instead of needing a new tool or plugin release per vertical.
3. **Intent routing and result fusion.** Per our docs, `/v1/search` routes the query to the best underlying sources by intent and then fuses and re-ranks the results — the caller does not pick an engine or merge result sets by hand.
4. **Region routing.** `zone: cn | intl` selects the result universe inside one API, instead of needing separate CN and global plugins.
5. **No-key first run.** Verified: an anonymous `POST /v1/search` returns `code: 0` with results, so a user can try the tool before creating an account.
6. **Low integration cost.** An MCP server is already live over Streamable HTTP at `https://api.anysearch.com/mcp` (anonymous or Bearer), and a Skill package already exists — the native tool plugin can be built and reviewed against a working endpoint rather than a spec.

**Questions for the maintainers** — we would rather ask before opening the PR:

1. **Category / overlap.** We could not find a published policy on category overlap (`CONTRIBUTING.md` is still `TODO`). Is another `search`-tagged provider welcome, or would you prefer it under a distinct tag or label to keep the category legible?
2. **Optional credentials.** Is an optional API key acceptable for a search-category provider, given that most existing providers require one? If not, we will make the key required and drop the anonymous path in the plugin.
3. **Risk classification.** `POST /v1/extract` fetches user-supplied URLs. Reading `docs/plugin-submission-requirements.md`, we believe that places the plugin at High risk ("proxy or crawl arbitrary URLs"). We intend to declare High and constrain inputs, set request timeouts, and avoid leaking credentials in errors. Please confirm that is the level you expect, and whether a High-risk plugin in the search category is acceptable.
4. **Exposed tag set.** The live catalog is broader than what a typical Dify user needs, and includes health, financial and legal data alongside some legally sensitive sources. We are happy to restrict the tag set the plugin exposes. Would you like us to, and do you have guidance on which verticals a search provider in the Marketplace should surface?
5. **Listing path.** We assume the expected route is a PR to `langgenius/dify-plugins` adding `anysearch/anysearch/anysearch-<version>.difypkg`, with `PRIVACY.md`, a source-repository link and an English README. If you would instead prefer to handle AnySearch as an official / featured integration, or an MCP-only listing, tell us and we will follow that path.

We are happy to adjust scope to whatever keeps the Marketplace coherent. Thanks.

https://anysearch.com/docs

issues.title: Kubernetes sandbox backend (no Docker socket)
issues.body:
## Problem

Every sandbox starts a sibling container through the `docker` CLI and
`/var/run/docker.sock`. That covers Agent Python tools and skills, the Code
node and its formatter, custom Playwright, MCP stdio, and the Codex and
OpenCode wrappers.

Some Kubernetes nodes have no Docker daemon: Talos, Bottlerocket,
containerd-only pools on EKS, AKS and GKE, and OpenShift. There, the only
choice is `HEYM_*_SANDBOX=subprocess`, which the docs call trusted
single-user only, or nothing. The Code node, Codex and OpenCode have no
fallback and fail.

## Who hits it

Anyone self-hosting Heym on Kubernetes, where mounting the host's Docker
socket is either impossible or not something you would want to do.

## Proposed approach

Three PRs, each releasable on its own:

1. **No behaviour change.** Move the nine `docker run` builders behind one
   `SandboxSpec` plus a `DockerRunner`. Parity tests assert that the argv
   stays the same, flag for flag. This also removes the five copies of
   `_docker_available`, `_resolve_image` and `_force_remove_container`.
2. **`HEYM_SANDBOX_BACKEND=kubernetes`, for the stdin/stdout-only sites:**
   the Python tool, the Code formatter, the Code node without requirements,
   and Playwright.
    - Each run is one Pod in a configurable namespace, under Pod Security
      `restricted`, with no ServiceAccount token.
    - `--network none|bridge` becomes a pod label that operator-provided
      NetworkPolicies select.
    - It is built on `httpx` and `websockets`, so there is no new dependency.
    - It fails closed exactly as the Docker path does.
3. **Workspaces.** Skills, Code node requirements and MCP stdio first, then
   Codex and OpenCode. There are two modes, and each run sees only its own
   files in both:
    - `stream` (default): a tar over the pod's attach stream, the same way
      `kubectl cp` moves files. No storage needed.
    - `volume`: an RWX PVC mounted with `subPath` set to the run's directory,
      the Kubernetes equivalent of today's `volume-subpath`.

Docker stays the default. No schema, migration, UI or public API changes.

## Touches

- `backend/app/services/*_executor.py`
- `mcp_stdio_sandbox.py`
- `playwright_sandbox.py`
- `code_formatter.py`
- `docker/heym-*-docker`
- `ENVIRONMENT-VARIABLES.md`

## Questions

1. Do you want a Kubernetes backend in-tree, or would you rather Docker stay
   the only supported sandbox?
2. Is the `SandboxSpec` plus runner shape right for PR 1? I'd rather agree on
   it here than in a large diff.
3. Codex's bubblewrap cannot run in a `restricted` pod. Is
   `--sandbox danger-full-access` acceptable when the pod is the boundary?
4. Would a Helm chart help, either in-tree under `deploy/helm/` or as a
   separate community chart on Artifact Hub? It would package Heym plus the
   sandbox namespace, RBAC and NetworkPolicies, with presets for OpenShift,
   EKS, AKS and GKE. I'd maintain it, including tag bumps.

I have a prototype that matches the current argv of all nine call sites and
am happy to share it. I'll wait for your go-ahead on scope, and can talk it
through on Discord first if that's easier.

issues.title: IPv6 address still in duplicate address detection is skipped and never retried
issues.body:
## Problem

A link-local IPv6 address that is still in duplicate address detection (DAD, "tentative") cannot be bound. `new_socket` treats `EADDRNOTAVAIL` as benign, logs a warning and returns `None`, so the interface gets no responder socket. `add_interface` then drops the multicast group membership it had just joined for that interface.

Nothing retries the bind. Once DAD finishes (about a second later) the address is usable, but the address set has not changed, so a caller that reconciles on address changes has no reason to call `async_update_interfaces` again. The instance stays without IPv6 on that interface until some unrelated address change.

## Where

- [`new_socket`](https://github.com/python-zeroconf/python-zeroconf/blob/4b6bd74a84d7f3382d5475a27ff7fd6ed0f4ceaf/src/zeroconf/_utils/net.py#L268-L274) returns `None` on `EADDRNOTAVAIL`.
- [`add_interface`](https://github.com/python-zeroconf/python-zeroconf/blob/4b6bd74a84d7f3382d5475a27ff7fd6ed0f4ceaf/src/zeroconf/_utils/net.py#L462-L480) drops the group membership when the responder socket could not be created.

This affects both construction (`create_sockets`) and `async_update_interfaces`.

## Reproduce

Start a container on an IPv6-enabled Docker network and construct `AsyncZeroconf(ip_version=IPVersion.All)` as soon as the process starts:

```
docker network create --ipv6 --subnet fd00:dead:beef::/64 zc6test
docker run --rm --network zc6test <image> python -c "..."
```

Log output:

```
WARNING zeroconf: Address not available when binding to ('fe80::943f:67ff:fe01:cbb8', 5353, 0, 11), it is expected to happen on some systems
```

The instance has an IPv4 sender only. Calling `async_update_interfaces()` a few seconds later binds the link-local sender.

Seen with 0.151.2 on Linux (arm64, Python 3.13). The same window exists whenever an interface comes up shortly before construction or a reconcile, for example at container or host boot.

## Suggested fix

Treat `EADDRNOTAVAIL` on an IPv6 address as retryable: remember the interfaces skipped for that reason and schedule one short internal retry (a few seconds), for both construction and `async_update_interfaces`.

Filtering tentative addresses up front is not an option, since `ifaddr` does not expose `IFA_F_TENTATIVE`.

## Workaround

esphome/device-builder#2864 runs one extra `async_update_interfaces` ten seconds after startup and after each binding change.

issues.title: Computer Use: confirm deadline and driver idle TTL follow-ups from #2838
issues.body:
Follow-up from #2838 (Computer Use driver session idle expiry). Report-only findings; nothing here blocks #2838.

## 1. A human confirm is bounded by the generic 300 s script deadline (P2)

- `vibe computer run` has no `--timeout`; every run uses `DEFAULT_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS = 300` (`vibe/computer_script_runner.py`). `avibe.confirm(...)` has no bound of its own, so a confirm waiting on a person gets whatever is left of that 300 s.
- The Controller already admits script connections up to 3600 s (`core/computer_script_sessions.py`, `_MAX_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT_SECONDS`).
- Live acceptance case: the owner did not see the prompt in time, and the script ended with `script_timeout` at step `avibe.confirm` (`ambiguous: true`).

Options: give confirm its own longer bound, or expose `--timeout` on `vibe computer run` up to the Controller ceiling.

## 2. A wait of more than 5 minutes retires the script's element tokens (P2, design together with 1)

- cua-driver 0.31.0 retires a named session after `DEFAULT_SESSION_IDLE_TTL = 5 min`. #2838 makes the Controller start the session again on the driver's pre-dispatch "session has ended" refusal, so Computer Use no longer dies for the Avibe Session.
- The driver still retires the earlier episode's element tokens and snapshots. A script that resumes after a confirm wait of more than 5 minutes therefore gets `observe_first` on its next input, so the SDK has to `waitFor` or observe again.
- A longer confirm bound alone would make this case common. Decide whether the SDK re-acquires its handles after a long `confirm`, whether the Controller keeps the driver session warm while a confirm is pending, or whether the confirm bound stays under the driver TTL.

issues.title: computer-use: launch() cannot reopen a running app's hidden main window
issues.body:
## Summary

When an app is running but its main window has been closed to the background, minimized, or the app is hidden (⌘H), Computer Use cannot bring the window back. `app.launch()` returns the pid but no window appears. `win.activate()` (`bring_to_front`) brings the process to the front without showing the window, and reports `bring_to_front_exact_window_unverified` (`process_activated=true, focused=false`). The owner has to click the Dock icon before any Agent can continue.

## Evidence (3.2.4rc1, owner machine, 2026-10-30)

Target: an Electron chat app (QQ) whose main window was put into each state below. Setup used only the window's own close and minimize buttons and app hide.

| Window state | Driver `launch_app` today | LaunchServices reopen without activation (`open -g -b <bundle_id>`) | Frontmost app afterwards |
|---|---|---|---|
| Closed to background | no on-screen window after 6 s | on screen in about 1.3 s | unchanged (Avibe) |
| Minimized | — | restored in about 1.3 s | unchanged |
| App hidden (⌘H) | — | restored in about 1.3 s | unchanged |
| On another Space | untested | untested | — |

## Root cause

At pinned `cua-driver-rs-v0.31.0` (`5272e492`), `launch_app` → `apps::launch_app` → `nsworkspace::open_application` sets `activates = false` and always attaches a synthetic `aevt/oapp` AppleEvent (`apps/nsworkspace.rs`). An app that is already running ignores `oapp`. A Dock click, or `open` on a running app, sends `aevt/rapp` (`kAEReopenApplication`) instead, and that event makes the app show its main window. Upstream `main` still has the same code path.

## Proposed fix

Patch the pinned driver: when the target app is already running, `launch_app` sends `kAEReopenApplication` instead of `oapp`. Keep `activates = false` and the existing focus-steal suppression, so the window comes back without taking the foreground.

- Tool name, schema, and description stay unchanged. The committed tool snapshot records the patch SHA-256, however, so its digest still moves. Follow the #3062 compatibility pattern: a newer Runtime also accepts the previous snapshot digest.
- Update `desktop/cua-driver/PATCHES.md`, `sources.json`, and `prepare-cua-driver.py` provenance.
- Add a deterministic AppKit fixture for the GUI acceptance: it hides its window on close and shows it again on reopen.
- Update the Computer Use Skill: when no on-screen window matches, call `app.launch()` once, then `app.waitFor({ onScreen: true })`. If no window appears, stop and ask the owner, as today. Never loop.
- Open the same fix upstream as a PR to trycua/cua, and add it to the patch's `upstream_refs` and upgrade plan.

## Acceptance

- Each of the three states above returns to the screen through `app.launch()`, and the previously frontmost app stays in front.
- First launch of a not-running app is unchanged.
- The driver tool snapshot is unchanged, or covered by compatibility tests.
- Live GUI check on the owner machine with a packaged build.

## Out of scope

- Foreground clicks that are ignored when the target window is not yet active: separate follow-up.
- Driver `unverifiable` click effects: by design, covered by the Skill since #3074.

issues.title: async_update_interfaces does not report whether the requested interfaces were bound
issues.body:
## Problem

`Zeroconf.async_update_interfaces` is best-effort and returns `None`, so a caller cannot tell whether the requested configuration was applied.

Two failure paths are logged and swallowed:

- A listen socket rebuild that fails, for example switching an IPv4 instance to `IPVersion.All` on a host that cannot open a dual-stack `AF_INET6` socket. The engine logs `Skipping interface update; listen socket rebuild failed` and returns `False`.
- A requested interface that fails to bind. The engine logs `Interface ... not added` once and carries on.

In both cases `Zeroconf.async_update_interfaces` still commits the requested `interfaces` and `ip_version` as the retained configuration, and returns normally.

## Where

- [Engine rebuild failure](https://github.com/python-zeroconf/python-zeroconf/blob/4b6bd74a84d7f3382d5475a27ff7fd6ed0f4ceaf/src/zeroconf/_engine.py#L179-L188) returns `False`, the same value as "nothing was added".
- [`_async_add_interface`](https://github.com/python-zeroconf/python-zeroconf/blob/4b6bd74a84d7f3382d5475a27ff7fd6ed0f4ceaf/src/zeroconf/_engine.py#L238-L256) returns `False` for an interface that did not come up.
- [`Zeroconf.async_update_interfaces`](https://github.com/python-zeroconf/python-zeroconf/blob/4b6bd74a84d7f3382d5475a27ff7fd6ed0f4ceaf/src/zeroconf/_core.py#L414-L457) uses the engine's result only to decide whether to re-announce.

## Why it matters

A caller that asks for dual-stack and cannot get it has no signal to fall back to `IPVersion.V4Only`, or to retry later. It also cannot log an accurate outcome: a caller that logs "reconciled with IPVersion.All" after a swallowed rebuild failure is wrong.

In esphome/device-builder#2864 this meant a runtime IPv4-only fallback could not be implemented, because the failure it would react to never surfaces.

## Suggested fix

Report the outcome from the public method. Options:

- Return whether the desired interface set fully bound, or the list of interfaces that were skipped.
- Raise when the address family rebuild fails, since in that case none of the requested change was applied.

Either keeps the best-effort behaviour for per-interface failures while letting callers react.

issues.title: [Previous Contributors Response Needed] Transition python-zeroconf to the Apache-2.0 License
issues.body:
## Why `python-zeroconf` sits under a long list of Python projects. #1123 asked for a permissive license in 2023, and the same request has reached me many times since, mostly in private conversations with developers in the Matter and smart home space. When #1123 was raised I discussed it with jstasiak, the only other active maintainer at the time, and [they agreed](https://github.com/python-zeroconf/python-zeroconf/issues/1123#issuecomment-1411451210) a permissive license would be fine for their contributions; this issue proposes Apache 2.0, one of the two licenses that request named. The LGPL's relinking requirement is deliberate: it guarantees users can swap in their own build of the library. That is easy for ordinary Python deployments and hard for frozen binaries and other sealed distributions (#276, #1363 and #1385 are all people shipping the library inside frozen executables, none of whom raised the license), so projects in those settings avoid the dependency or go without. In practice it mostly gets lumped into a blanket no-LGPL policy rather than weighed on its own, and projects only notice when it becomes a problem, so little of this is public; an example is OpenVoiceOS's license checks flagging the dependency (OpenVoiceOS/ovos-core#546). As maintainer, my call is that this protection is not worth the users it costs. The change has a price too: some contributors declined, and all of their surviving expression had to be removed and replaced (tracked below, down to a disclosed set of single-statement lines any implementation would share). issues.title: Link-local AAAA records stay unscoped on a dual-stack host: the scoped IPv6 copy is dropped as a duplicate of the IPv4 one (follow-up to #1567)
issues.body:
#1764 made `parsed_scoped_addresses()` prefer a scoped copy of an AAAA record when an unscoped one is also cached, and left "the IPv4-only-arrival case" for a follow-up. I couldn't find an issue for that follow-up, so here it is with measurements. In short: on a dual-stack host the scoped copy usually never reaches the cache, so #1764 has nothing to prefer. Disabling packet duplicate suppression is enough for 0.151.5 to return `fe80::…%<idx>`.

## Setup

- **Querier:** Linux 6.12, 32-bit ARM (armv7l), Python 3.14. One wired interface (index 2) with IPv4, a link-local address, and global and ULA IPv6 addresses (SLAAC, with temporary addresses). `AsyncZeroconf(ip_version=IPVersion.All)`, default interfaces.
- **Peers:** embedded devices on the same link. Each answers with its A record and three AAAA records (link-local, global, ULA) in one message, over both IPv4 and IPv6.
- **Version:** 0.151.5, and master at f0c27b38 (2026-10-01), whose `src/zeroconf` is identical to 0.151.5. Both were run as pure Python so `AsyncListener._process_datagram_at_time` could be wrapped. For every response carrying a peer's link-local AAAA, the wrapper logged which socket it arrived on, the sender's address, and the scope zeroconf would give it. It logged before the duplicate check runs.
- **Control:** a plain IPv6 UDP socket on 5353, joined to ff02::fb on interface 2, sent an AAAA query. All 18 peers answered by multicast from their `fe80::` address, and `recvfrom` gave scope 2 for every one. The peers do their part, and the kernel supplies the scope.

## Results

**One-shot lookups:** `AddressResolver(host).async_request(zc, 3000)`, a fresh instance each time, 10 rounds over 3 peers (0.151.5).

| Measurement | 0.151.5 |
|---|---|
| Lookups where `parsed_scoped_addresses()` gave a usable link-local scope | 0 / 30 |
| IPv6 respond socket bound to a global address, not link-local | 30 / 30 |
| First copy of the link-local AAAA in an IPv4 packet (scope `None`) | 14 |
| First copy by unicast IPv6 from the peer's global address (scope 0) | 16 |
| A scoped copy (from the peer's `fe80::`, scope 2) received at all | 1 |
| ...that ended up in the cache | 0 |

In that one lookup, the IPv4 copy arrived on the `::` listen socket from v4-mapped `::ffff:192.0.2.x` (scope 0) at 571 ms. The IPv6 copy from the peer's `fe80::` address (scope 2) followed at 573 ms. The cache ended with only the scope-0 and `None` entries.

**Browsing:** an `AsyncServiceBrowser` for the peers' service type, with the cache read every 10 s.

- **Unmodified (0.151.5, 300 s):** the link-local addresses stayed unscoped throughout.
- **0.151.5 with `_DUPLICATE_PACKET_SUPPRESSION_INTERVAL = 0`, otherwise unchanged:** the same pair (v4-mapped first, `fe80::` 4 ms later) arrived at 202 s for all three peers. From then on the cache held a scope-2 entry for each, and `parsed_scoped_addresses()` returned `fe80::…%2` for all three.

**Duplicate drops on master:** a 300 s browse with debug logging logged 43 "Ignoring duplicate message" lines for packets from the peers' `fe80::` addresses. Those are the only copies that carry a scope. It also logged 183 for v4-mapped senders. All were on the `::` socket.

## Why: four ways the scope is lost

1. **Duplicate suppression ignores the sender.** The IPv6 listen socket is bound to `::` with `IPV6_V6ONLY` off, so it receives both IPv4 and IPv6 multicast. A peer's IPv4 and IPv6 announcements are byte-identical, and the IPv4 copy usually arrives first. The listener's duplicate checks compare payload bytes only: both the last-packet check and the `_recent_packets` cache from #1750. So the IPv6 copy, the only one that carries a scope, is dropped. #1750 keeps that state per listener "so a duplicate seen on one interface does not suppress" a packet arriving on another. But with the dual-stack `::` socket, the IPv4 and IPv6 sides of one interface share a listener. #1764 can't help, because the scoped record never reaches the cache.
2. **The IPv4 copy is scoped from its sender.** On the `::` socket it arrives as `::ffff:a.b.c.d` with scope 0. That gives a cache entry with scope 0, which is no more usable than one with none.
3. **The first answer comes over IPv4, unicast.** The first query is QU, so the peer answers by unicast to the query's source address, and an IPv4 answer carries the AAAA records too. It arrives on the IPv4 respond socket, so it has no scope, although that socket belongs to one interface.
4. **The IPv6 respond socket is bound to a global address.** zeroconf binds one IPv6 respond socket per interface, to one of the interface's addresses. Here it was always a global one (which one varied between runs), never the link-local. So a QU answer over IPv6 comes from the peer's global address, and the scope taken from that sender is 0.

## The RFCs

- **RFC 6762 §6.2:** a responder "MUST include all addresses that are valid on the interface on which it is sending the message". The RFC's example is a link-local plus a routable address, "so that queriers receive both and can make their own choice", and it says this "allows a querier that only has an IPv6 link-local address to connect to the link-local address". The same section says a responder SHOULD include the other address type in the additional section, so that "all a device's addresses are delivered atomically in a single message". An AAAA record arriving in an IPv4 packet (cases 1 to 3) is therefore normal, conformant behaviour, not an edge case.
- **RFC 6762 §14:** addresses in responses "MUST be valid for use on the interface on which the response is being sent", and a host needs "network programming APIs that allow applications ... to discover on what interface a Multicast DNS response was received". So a link-local address in a response belongs to the interface the response arrived on. For the respond sockets that interface is known, since each is bound to one. The shared `::` listen socket serves every interface, so there it isn't known. Either way, the sender's sockaddr only gives the interface when the sender happens to be link-local.
- **RFC 6762 §5.4:** the first questions are QU, and "a responder SHOULD usually respond with a unicast packet directed back to the querier". That is why the first answer arrives unicast, on whichever family and source address the query went out from (cases 3 and 4).
- **RFC 6762 §20:** a dual-stack host "acts like a multihomed host, with one connection to the logical 'IPv4 Ethernet segment', and a connection to the logical 'IPv6 Ethernet segment'". On that view an IPv4 and an IPv6 copy of the same answer are two separate arrivals, not a duplicate packet (case 1).
- **RFC 4007 §6 and §11.2:** a non-global address needs a zone index, and zone 0 or no zone means the default zone. Linux has no default zone for link-local addresses, so connecting to `fe80::…` or `fe80::…%0` fails with `EINVAL`. A cache entry with scope 0 is as unusable as one with none.

## Possible fixes

Roughly from smallest to largest:

- **Key duplicate suppression on the scope the packet's records would get** (`addrs[3]`, 0 otherwise), so the scoped IPv6 copy of an answer isn't dropped behind the unscoped IPv4 one (case 1). This looks like the change that would matter most in practice. The control above shows it's enough for #1764 to work whenever a peer multicasts over IPv6. PR #1926 does this.
- **Don't scope records from a v4-mapped sender** (case 2). Those packets are IPv4, and scope 0 means "unknown".
- **Bind the per-interface IPv6 respond socket to the interface's link-local address** (case 4). QU answers over IPv6 then come from the peer's link-local address, with the right scope.
- **Scope link-local AAAA records from the receiving interface**, IPv4 packets included (case 3), as RFC 6762 §14 describes. The draft #1568 ("Use per-interface per-protocol sockets") does this: one socket per interface and per address family, each listener stamping its interface index on what it receives, and IPv6 bound to link-local. That would also cover cases 1, 2 and 4. The alternative #1567 mentions is `IP_PKTINFO`/`IPV6_RECVPKTINFO` with `recvmsg`.

Our workaround in the meantime is to derive the scope ourselves: the interface whose IPv4 subnet or IPv6 prefix contains one of the peer's other addresses.

We'd be glad to help further, including running any patched build (#1568 rebased, for instance) against the same peers with the same measurements.
